exposure: publication of national guidelines to support physiologic labor and reduce medical interventions
Publication of national guidelines to support physiologic labor and reduce medical interventions
outcome: Neonatal outcomes (umbilical artery pH < 7.10, neonatal transfers)
cohort: Women who had no prior cesarean delivery and gave birth after 37 weeks of gestation to a singleton fetus in cephalic presentation after spontaneous labor in 2016 (before) and 2018 (after) in a type IIb perinatal center in France
finding: The reduction of active interventions during labor, following the publication of national guidelines, was associated with a longer duration of labor and a decrease in the rates of cesarean births, postpartum hemorrhages, and neonatal transfers.
mod_finding: The reduction of active interventions during labor was associated with a decrease in the rates of cesarean births.
